title: Gemcitabine and capecitabine after pancreatic surgery
context_label: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma after macroscopically complete resection
schedule_label: Gemcitabine on days 1, 8, 15. Take capecitabine twice daily on days 1–21, then seven tablet-free days. Up to six 28-day cycles.
schedule_summary: Gemcitabine on days 1, 8, 15. Take capecitabine twice daily on days 1–21, then seven tablet-free days. Up to six 28-day cycles.
purpose: After surgery has removed all visible pancreatic cancer, treatment aims to reduce the risk of the cancer returning.
indication_text: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma after macroscopically complete resection
administration_text: Gemcitabine runs over 30 minutes. Swallow prescribed capecitabine tablets whole with water, with food or within 30 minutes of a meal. Follow the dated tablet calendar.
monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney and liver tests on day 1. Repeat blood counts on days 8 and 15.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: It interferes with copying DNA as cells divide. Blood-forming cells can also be affected.
agents.mechanism: It interferes with copying DNA as cells divide. Blood-forming cells can also be affected.
agents.watch: Phone promptly about fever, bleeding, a new cough or difficulty breathing.
visual: It interferes with copying DNA as cells divide. Blood-forming cells can also be affected.
consent_risks: Call promptly for fever, shivering, unexplained bruises or bleeding.
Contact oncology urgently for new breathlessness, reduced urine or a painful blistering rash.

agents.name: Capecitabine
agents.explanation: The body converts capecitabine into fluorouracil, which disrupts DNA and RNA processes needed for cell growth. Tablets are active chemotherapy; taking them at home still requires a clear monitoring and interruption plan.
agents.watch: Stop tablets and contact the team for significant diarrhoea, painful mouth ulcers, hand-foot soreness affecting activities, fever or dehydration. Chest pain needs urgent assessment. Do not restart until instructed.
risks: Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity
consent_risks: Hold tablets and call for significant diarrhoea, painful mouth ulcers or hands and feet painful enough to limit activity.
Chest pain or severe early symptoms
Chest pain needs emergency assessment. Severe early diarrhoea, dehydration or fever needs urgent oncology review.

common_effects.title: Eating and drinking
common_effects.text: Tell the team about nausea or reduced appetite. Call if you cannot keep fluids down.

common_effects.title: Fatigue and low counts
common_effects.text: Rest between activities. Report fever, breathlessness or unusual bleeding promptly.

common_effects.title: Hands and feet
common_effects.text: Report sore, red or peeling skin before it limits walking or using your hands.

serious_effects.title: Infection
serious_effects.text: Fever, shivering or sudden illness: phone oncology immediately.

serious_effects.title: Urgent symptoms
serious_effects.text: Seek urgent help for chest pain, trouble breathing or collapse.

serious_effects.title: Bowel symptoms
serious_effects.text: Ring promptly for persistent diarrhoea, dehydration or severe abdominal pain.

support.title: Pancreatic and biliary symptoms
support.text: Ask the team about a new fever with jaundice, dark urine or shivering, especially if you have a bile duct stent.

evidence.title: ESPAC-4
evidence.interpretation: After resection, gemcitabine plus capecitabine improved median overall survival compared with gemcitabine alone (28.0 versus 25.5 months in the original analysis).
evidence.limitations: These are group results from the named setting. They cannot predict the benefit or side effects for an individual.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.timing: Up to three times daily if needed; at least 6 hours apart. Maximum 30 mg or 0.5 mg/kg per day, whichever is lower, for up to 5 days.

prescription_notes: Use for this visit. Reconcile any rescue medicines already supplied.

local_adjuncts.directions: Rinse 1 mL around the mouth four times daily after meals during the chemotherapy regimen.
Rinse 10 mL around the mouth for at least 1 minute four times daily; expel after rinsing.
Take one tablet three times daily as required.
Take 4 mg after the first episode of diarrhoea, then 2 mg after each further episode, to a maximum of 16 mg/day.
